column1: # The closed dictionary of the kinds of code checks.
# Public, in the model input. The rows of a lesson are
# Platform/<lesson>/forms/code-rules.tsv with the columns id, kind, name, args, stage, norm; a row names a kind of this dictionary and carries no expected
# answer. The product generation cycle checks the lesson rows by one common interpreter that holds no literal of a lesson; the acceptance does not
# read them. This
# dictionary is not the closed dictionary of the judge engine (spec/acceptance.norms.md): the names do not mix (addendum (39) item 7).
# name: what the profile field code (PROFILE.md) maps the name of a row to — package: the import path of a package of the main module of the candidate, as
# go list prints it; function, type: <import path>#<identifier>, a top-level function or type of that package (# because an import path may hold dots).
# Rows of one lesson with the same name use kinds of the same name type. args: one JSON object on one line with exactly the fields of the kind; a path names a
# file of the specification export, relative to its root (the directory that holds Platform/). The interpreter reads the candidate by go list, go/parser,
# go/ast and go/types and neither builds nor runs it. The files of a package are those go list names for the default build context of the stand: GoFiles
# and CgoFiles are its nontest files, TestGoFiles and XTestGoFiles its test files. The stand also runs the tests of the candidate; that run is not a code check.
# A string literal is an interpreted or raw string literal of Go, compared by its value.
# Outcome of a row: holds, or fails with a mechanical message — the id of the row, the symbol and the clause of check that does not hold. A kind outside this dictionary, args outside the
# fields of the kind, a path that is not a file of the export, a stage outside stages.tsv or two name types for one name is a data error of the lesson
# (prep_failed), not a skip. A name without a mapping in the field code, or a mapping that does not resolve to a symbol of the name type,
# fails the row as no mapping. Which rows a stage requires: the gate code:* of forms/stages.tsv of the lesson.
# check: the clauses all hold.
kind
pure_core
column4: Walk the imports of the package without its tests from the package itself, descending into every package that is not a leaf. Leaves: the packages of the standard library and the packages of a pinned module; their own imports do not count. A pinned module is a module that a require directive of Platform/common/versions/go.mod names without the comment // indirect; the module of a package is the one go list names for it; a module that only an indirect require names is not pinned and is walked like any other. No direct import of a visited package equals an entry of forbid or begins with an entry followed by /; a leaf counts as such an import of the package that imports it. See [Requirements of the course to code](../PROFILE.md#requirements-of-the-course-to-code).

column1: step_form
column4: The symbol is a top-level function without a receiver and without type parameters, with exactly two parameters and exactly two results; the type of the first parameter is identical (go/types) to the type of the first result; the type of the second result is a slice. With core: the package of the function is the package that the field code maps core to, and core is the name of a pure_core row of the same lesson. See [Requirements of the course to code](../PROFILE.md#requirements-of-the-course-to-code).

column1: table_driven
column4: A //go:embed directive of a nontest file of the package matches a file whose bytes equal the bytes of the form at the path. No string literal of the nontest files of the package has a value equal to a cell of the form of at least min_cell characters (Unicode code points); the cells of the form are the fields, separated by TAB, of its lines other than the lines that begin with #, the header line included. See [Requirements of the course to code](../PROFILE.md#requirements-of-the-course-to-code).

column1: property_tests
column4: A test file of the package of the function has a top-level function TestXxx(t *testing.T) whose body calls Check or CheckEqual of the standard package testing/quick, named by its import in that file, with a function argument that is the symbol or a function literal whose body calls the symbol. The test is not run by this check; whether it passes is the outcome of the run of the tests of the candidate by the stand. A property package outside the standard library does not count.

column1: exhaustive
column4: The symbol is a defined type whose underlying type is an integer or string basic type. The number of package-level constants of exactly that type equals the number of distinct values of the column in the form: the lines after the header line, other than the lines that begin with #; a cell - is not a value. Every expression switch of the nontest files of the packages of the main module whose tag has that type lists all those constants in its case clauses, or has a default clause whose body calls panic.

column1: requires_module
column4: The go.mod of the main module of the candidate has a require directive of the module with exactly the version that the go.mod at from requires, and no replace directive of the module; the root of the main module holds no go.work and no vendor directory. The imports of the package without its tests (go list -deps) hold a package of the module that a package of the main module among them imports under a name other than _ and uses by at least one qualified identifier.

column1: complexity
column4: Each function of the symbol — the function itself, or every function declaration and function literal of the nontest files of the package — has at most max_branches branches and at most max_lines lines. Branches: the nodes of its body of kind if, for and range, each case clause of a switch or type switch and each communication clause of a select other than the default clause, and each binary && and ||; the nodes of a nested function literal count to that literal, not to the enclosing function. Lines: the physical lines of its body from the line of the opening brace to the line of the closing brace, both included. See [Requirements of the course to code](../PROFILE.md#requirements-of-the-course-to-code).
